Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **5** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0fb55fc2fca5590a76c1827d95bf7d1bacf22d02` → `packageMentionDocs`.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `ba08362c27a52033c9472ccf01769b0afc74bea8`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #23255 (body, triage `6147649246`, claim `6178215554`, os-dev report `6179984024`), PR #23551 (body, 4-file list, net diff `origin/main...ba08362c27` = 3 commits: `6cc6f290ab`, `40e6510ac1`, merge `ba08362c27`; the diff touches only `.changeset/23255-verify-flows-system-arm.md`, `packages/verify/README.md`, `packages/verify/src/handle.ts`, `packages/verify/src/handle.flows-system-start.test.ts`), the check-runs on the head, and the runtime / engine / trigger source at the head for the mechanism claims.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies (all in `@objectstack/verify`):**

1. `VerifyHandle.flows.run` gains a second overload `run(name, params, opts: AsSystem)` resolving a `FlowRun` beside the unchanged `run(name, params, opts: AsUser)`. Widening of the accept-set of one method; nothing removed. **Right.** It mirrors `hooks.run`'s existing overload pair over one implementation branching on `namesSystem(opts, door)`; the implementation signature is annotated `opts: AsUser | AsSystem` exactly as `hooks.run`'s is.
2. Types reachable through the overload: `AsSystem` (`{ system: true }`, existing, TSDoc widened to name `flows.run`), `EngineRow` (existing), `FlowRun = AutomationResult & { flowName }` (existing, unchanged). No new exported type, no new error shape. **Right.**
3. `{ as, system: true }` together: refused `INVALID_REQUEST` / `400` before any dispatch, through the same `namesSystem` → `callShapeRefusal` path `hooks.run` uses (`handle.ts` `callShapeRefusal` sets `code: 'INVALID_REQUEST', status: 400, statusCode: 400`). Pinned in the new suite. **Right.**
4. The `{ as }` overload is unchanged: the only edit to that arm is the `(opts as AsUser).as` narrowing cast; it still dispatches `POST /automation/:name/trigger` through `HttpDispatcher` with the bearer only. Its TSDoc gains a paragraph saying a self-triggered `runAs: 'system'` flow is refused there for every caller including the platform admin, which is what `refusesElevatedSelfTriggeredStart` does (`isSystem` is never set on inbound HTTP). Pinned 6 ways (3 flows × member/admin → `VerifyRefusal`, `PERMISSION_DENIED` / `403`, 0 rows, 0 runs). **Right.**
5. No runtime file, HTTP door or admission rule changed: `git diff origin/main...head -- packages/runtime packages/services packages/triggers packages/rest` is empty. `flow-start-admission.ts`, `domains/automation.ts`, `action-execution.ts`, `endpoint-executor.ts` untouched. **Right**, and matches the triage direction's ⛔ (no HTTP door starts a flow as the system principal).
6. Mechanism: the system arm calls `kernel.getServiceAsync('automation')` (the same accessor the existing `automation.evaluateCondition` door uses, typed `AutomationEngine`) then `automation.execute(name, { params: { ...(params ?? {}) }, callerParamKeys: [] })` and returns `{ ...result, flowName: name }`. Verified against `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts` at the head: `activateFlowTrigger` hands every trigger the callback that calls `this.execute(flowName, ctx)` (engine.ts ~4025), so the arm is the trigger's own call. **Right.**
7. Context fidelity vs a real tick: `schedule-trigger.ts` builds `{ event: 'schedule', ...(organization !== null ? { tenantId } : {}), params: { jobId, flowName, schedule }, callerParamKeys: [] }`. The arm builds `{ params, callerParamKeys: [] }`. Same shape class (seeds as `params`, empty caller-key list, no user, no positions/permissions); the two omissions (`event`, so the run-history row records the engine default `'manual'` per engine.ts ~1188 `type: context?.event ?? 'manual'`; and the binding's `tenantId`) are stated in the TSDoc, README and changeset. **Right as documented; fidelity gap acknowledged, not a defect.**
8. The dev's claim that the tick context carries no `executionContext` and the admission predicate is asked only at the by-name doors: verified. `AutomationContext` (`packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`) has no `executionContext` field at all; `refusesElevatedSelfTriggeredStart` is called from exactly three runtime sites (`domains/automation.ts:1861` trigger route, `action-execution.ts:1185`, `endpoint-executor.ts:564`) and nowhere in `engine.ts`; `engine.execute` never reads `isSystem`. So the in-process `execute` call needs and takes no system execution context, exactly as the tick. **Right.**
9. Returned `FlowRun` is what `flows.resume(run: FlowRunRef, ...)` takes back (`FlowRunRef = { flowName; runId? }`); the engine's `AutomationResult` carries `runId` for a paused run, the arm adds `flowName`. Pinned: a `screen` flow started `{ system: true }` resolves `status: 'paused'` with a string `runId`, then `flows.resume(run, ..., { as: admin })` lands the write. **Right.** (`flows.resume` stays `AsUser`-only; resume is not a start door, so admission is not consulted there.)
10. Failure dialect (the dev's open question, judged in ③): the system arm resolves with `execute`'s own result (`success: false`, `code: 'FLOW_DISABLED'` for a disabled flow; `success: false` with no `code` and `error: "Flow 'x' not found"` for an unknown name, engine.ts ~6494; `status: 'failed'` for a dispatched run that failed). The `{ as }` arm rejects for the same situations because the route runs `classifyFlowRefusal` and `flowIsUnknown` first. The asymmetry is accurately described in the TSDoc, README and changeset. **Right as described.**
11. Negative controls and ablation are real-engine measurements (ledger object nobody but the admin may write; run-log count), 15 cases, ablation showed 8 red / 7 green with the branch skipped. Not re-run here (read-only); accepted as the PR's own evidence, consistent with the diff.
12. Documentation surface: README gains the usage block and the principal-model paragraph; header design-rules comment in `handle.ts` gains the `flows.run(..., { system: true })` entry. No API-surface baseline file exists for `packages/verify` (package holds `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`, `package.json`, tsconfigs, `vitest.config.ts`, `src/`), so there is none to update. **Right.**

One observation, not a finding: a flow declared (or defaulting to) `runAs: 'user'` started with `{ system: true }` reaches the engine with no `userId`, and the engine then logs its "executes with runAs:'user' but its trigger resolved no user" warning (engine.ts ~6410) exactly as a real tick on such a flow would. That is tick-faithful behaviour and the TSDoc's "the engine applies the flow's own runAs" covers it; no change asked.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/23255-verify-flows-system-arm.md`: `'@objectstack/verify': minor`, headed `feat(verify): ...`, carrying `Clause-②: yes`, with a before/after usage block and the failure-dialect paragraph. The diff publishes a purely additive widening (a new overload on a published method, no removal, no renamed export) of `@objectstack/verify` (`18.0.0-next.1`), and the only package whose `packages/**/src/**` moved is `@objectstack/verify`, so under the ruling mechanised in `check-changeset-no-major.mjs` (a declared widening grades at least one moved package `minor`+) `minor` is the correct level and the only moved package carries it. No ADR-0087 registration is owed (nothing breaking, no metadata moved). `Check Changeset` on the head: success. **Clause-②: yes (widening)** — matches the PR body's `Clause-②: yes` line and the triage grade.

- **Dev flag — `deviations[0]`** (one `vitest run` escaped the verify lock for ~2 min, killed by PID, output discarded; the reported full-suite figure is the earlier locked run): a process-hygiene deviation with no effect on the diff or the head's check-runs. **Answered: no action.**
- **Dev flag — `deviations[1]`** (commit trailers carry the repo's model-free pair rather than the harness's model-named trailer): conforms to AGENTS.md; outside this record's remit. **Answered: no action.**
- **Dev flag — gate not measured** (`pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 3 PREREQUISITE NOT MET, unbuilt packages outside the diff): left to CI as the report says. The head's `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Lint · ESLint`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Type Check · workspace` / `source gates` / `consumer gates` / `debt ledger`, and `Test Core (1/6 … 6/6)` were **in progress** at brief time (read once, no watcher). Completed and green on the head: `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Check PR Size`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `No other open PR may claim the same issue`, `No other open PR may claim the same single-writer path`, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, `The card this PR closes must claim this branch`, `Auto Label`, `filter`. Skipped (not applicable): `Build Docs`, `Console Pin Gate`, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` shards, `Packed-tarball smoke`, `Temporal Conformance`. Nothing failed. The merge queue's own branch protection still waits on the in-progress families; this record does not pre-empt them.
- **`open_questions[0]` — failure dialect of the system arm (A shipped: resolve with the engine's `success: false`; `{ as }` rejects).** Judged on the inputs: **shipping A without a ruling is correct and safe to land.** Reasons: (a) it is the only answer that keeps the handle's stated design rule ("returns what that door returned") and the arm's whole premise (this IS the trigger's callback, which receives a result, never a throw, engine.ts ~4025–4040 handles `FLOW_DISABLED` / missing-flow / `status: 'failed'` as result arms); (b) the engine's own classification is preserved whole (`code: 'FLOW_DISABLED'`, `status: 'failed'`, `error` naming the flow), so no information is lost and nothing is invented; (c) B would widen `@objectstack/runtime`'s public surface (export `classifyFlowRefusal` / `flowIsUnknown`) outside the claimed file surface and needs its own Clause-② card, and C mints a third kit error shape — both are rulings, not reviewer choices, and neither is required for the card's ask (the three pins the triage direction names all hold). On the typo hazard: a typo'd flow name resolves `success: false`, no `code`, `error` containing the name, and 0 runs; it passes silently only in a test that asserts neither `success` nor any side effect of the flow, and such a test proves nothing about the flow with either dialect. The contract is unmistakable at all three reading points: the overload's TSDoc (one full paragraph ending "assert on `success` (and `status`) before asserting on the flow's side effects"), the README usage block (`expect(sweep.success).toBe(true)` with the sentence saying why), and the changeset ("Assert on `success` before asserting on the flow's side effects"), and the new suite pins all three result arms (failed run, unknown name, paused run). **Residual for the maintainer, not a blocker:** one method now carries two failure dialects; if a single dialect is wanted, that is a follow-up card on the runtime surface (option B's shape), to be filed after this lands. HotCRM's migration needs the one `expect(run.success)` assertion the report names.
- **Out-of-scope findings (carrier: none, as reported):** the `event` / organization fidelity gap is documented in TSDoc (see ① item 7); the `automation-trigger-elevated-door.test.ts` system row measuring the route's hand-set `{ isSystem: true }` arm is a different claim and is rightly left alone. **Answered: no escalation.**
- No `needs-user-decision` is owed by this record. No comment on the card or PR reads as a ruling against A.
